title: GTA San Andreas: Alternate Timelines
subtitle: A state-sized gang war where loyalty is more expensive than bullets.

achievements.title: Avenue King
achievements.description: Take the whole state block by block.

achievements.title: Family First
achievements.description: Win by keeping your original crew together.

achievements.title: Casino Phantom
achievements.description: Use Venturas money to buy peace.

achievements.title: Witness Deal
achievements.description: Trade the war for federal survival.

achievements.title: Dust Runner
achievements.description: Leave with cash before the state buries you.

homecoming.title: Welcome Back to Ganton Heights
text: You come home to a neighborhood that still remembers your name and has already used it in three arguments this morning.
The corner store has bars on the windows, fresh graffiti on the shutters, and a clerk who asks if you want cigarettes, lottery tickets, or plausible deniability.
Your old set says the city changed while you were gone. Translation: everyone got greedier, the cops got louder, and the funerals got better catering.
A police chopper circles overhead like it is reading subtitles for your life. Welcome home.

choices.label: Start with family and gather street truth
Arm up and hit rival corners immediately
Call a fixer and map the legal battlefield

old_friends.title: Old Friends, New Prices
text: Your childhood crew meets you at a backyard barbecue where half the guests are armed and the other half are pretending they are not.
Big Smoke-style talkers promise empire, gym-rat lieutenants promise discipline, and one cousin promises to stop gambling after just one more horse race. Nobody believes him.
The table goes quiet when someone asks whether you want respect, revenge, or retirement. In this state you only get to pick two.

choices.label: Rebuild neighborhood protection first
Skip small wars and chase Venturas cash

neighborhood_fire.title: Neighborhood on Fire
text: Two blocks flip in one night, three in the morning, and by lunchtime a radio host calls you a civic revitalization program with assault rifles.
Rivals push back hard. You win the streets but lose sleep, patience, and one very expensive lowrider.
Kids cheer your name while grandmothers curse your tactics from porch chairs that have seen five generations of bad decisions.
You can escalate, negotiate, or pivot to bigger games before the city writes your obituary in advance.

choices.label: Open desert gun-running routes
Take a meeting with city hall intermediaries

badge_or_street.title: Badge or Street
text: A narcotics detective with polished shoes and filthy morals offers a simple arrangement: feed him selective rivals and he feeds you selective freedom.
He smiles like a used-car salesman who just discovered extortion. You hate him instantly, which in this city is usually the beginning of a profitable partnership.
Your crew wants blood, not paperwork, but blood tends to come with helicopters and headlines.

choices.label: Play the detective and weaponize his badge
Reject the badge and build pure street power

desert_run.title: Desert Run
text: Out past the city limits, the desert is all dust, biker compounds, and conspiracy radio channels explaining how pigeons are government equipment.
You broker ammo with meth bikers who call everyone brother and still check your pockets before hugging you.
One bad deal can get you buried where tumbleweeds do the witness statements, but one good deal can arm an entire county.
The bikers demand either fear or respect. Unfortunately both are sold as separate packages.

choices.label: Pay fair and earn biker respect
Steal their cache and outrun consequences

casino_tables.title: Venturas Tables
text: Venturas glows like a tax write-off for sin itself. Slot machines scream, whales gamble, and every casino owner pretends organized crime is an urban legend with valet service.
You make alliances with card dealers, pit bosses, and one magician who definitely launders money between rabbit tricks.
By midnight your operation has clean income, dirty enemies, and a stack of chips that smells like victory and stale smoke.

choices.label: Use casino cash to buy city hall leverage
Move profits back into neighborhood muscle

biker_treaty.title: Biker Treaty
text: The desert clubhouse summit includes burnt coffee, loaded shotguns, and a handwritten peace treaty on the back of a monster truck flyer.
Your lieutenant says trust no one. The biker boss says trust everyone. Both men are lying in different accents.
If you unify these maniacs, the whole state opens. If you insult them, your convoy becomes a bonfire with ambitions.

choices.label: Forge the alliance and combine forces
Sell treaty intel to city hall

city_hall_deal.title: City Hall Deal
text: Behind polished doors, elected officials discuss ethics the way mechanics discuss ballet: politely and with zero intention of participating.
They offer contracts, zoning advantages, and quiet immunity if you keep the violence photogenic and mostly off downtown streets.
Your crew hates this. The accountants love it. History says accountants usually win in the long run, but history has terrible taste.

choices.label: Sign and become the legal-looking power
Burn the deal and declare open war
Take a secret federal immunity deal

final_turf_war.title: Statewide Turf War
text: The final week is chaos with branding: freeway ambushes, courtroom stunts, and neighborhood rallies that look like political campaigns sponsored by body armor.
Everyone wants your crown, your contracts, or your funeral plot. Sometimes all three.
You can rule through fear, rule through family, cash out before the storm, or let the whole empire collapse under its own ego.

choices.label: Take every district by force and claim the crown
Defend your core crew and hold fewer but loyal blocks
Liquidate assets and vanish through Venturas
Overextend into every enemy front at once

ending_avenue_king.title: Avenue King
text: You own the map, the ports, and the panic. The state runs on your schedule now.
The victory parade is unofficial, heavily armed, and somehow still better organized than local government.

ending.title: Avenue King
ending.summary: You conquer San Aurelio and build an empire too big to ignore.

ending_family_first.title: Family First
text: You keep fewer districts, but the ones you hold are loyal and profitable.
Nobody calls you a king. They call you something rarer in this business: trustworthy.

ending.title: Family First
ending.summary: You win without sacrificing your people for one more zip code.

ending_federal_pawn.title: Federal Pawn
text: The immunity deal keeps your heartbeat steady and your conscience unemployed.
You survive, testify, and watch your old world burn from behind very expensive government curtains.

ending.title: Federal Pawn
ending.summary: You trade the street throne for protection and paperwork.

ending_dust_runner.title: Dust Runner
text: You cash out before anyone can pin you down. By sunrise, the state only has rumors and unpaid parking tickets.
Some call it cowardice. Your offshore account calls it excellent decision-making.

ending.title: Dust Runner
ending.summary: You disappear rich while everyone else keeps fighting over your old corners.

ending_ashes_of_avenue.title: Ashes of the Avenue
text: You try to hold every street at once and lose all of them in a week of sirens and smoke.
The city survives. Your legacy does not.

ending.title: Ashes of the Avenue
ending.summary: Greed outruns strategy and the empire implodes.
